bullets: Game 4 of 4 in a Hero Berserker deck-showcase video; each game is a different deck, and this one is the bait list - "We're in the next match here guys with this bait deck. Honestly, I was always really curious about how the Berserker would go with bait because of the nerf to the spirits" (t=661-670s).

Piloted as log bait with constant two-lane pressure: Goblin Barrel at the enemy tower ((14, 26)/(14, 25)/(14, 24) then (3, 25)/(3, 26)), Wall Breakers at the bridge ((8, 14), (4, 14), (14, 14), (13, 14)) and a spirit escorting the barrel, while Berserker, Dart Goblin, Tesla and Royal Delivery hold his own half. His own summary of the plan at clock 0:23: "I just want to keep on spamming the scouts."

Against a near-mirror bait deck he is out-cycled through regular time ("I feel like we're going to get out-cycled though. We aren't really in the greatest cycle right now to defend like wall breakers", clock 2:00-1:57; "I need to get out of this cycle, man", clock 0:42) and answers by chipping rather than defending cleanly - "I do want to be really annoying, get as much damage as possible in return cuz we are in a bad spot" (clock 0:52-0:48).

The hero is the defensive trump the deck otherwise lacks: two Savage Survival activations (clock 2:40 and 1:45) hold pushes a 2.4-elixir bait list could not otherwise stop - "Oh my god, what an ability right there. Taking out his Berserker and nearly the dark goblin."

The spirit nerf is the recurring cost: he drops a Fire Spirit at the bridge out of habit at clock 1:33 and it never connects ("Dude, I'm an idiot"), and he rules that spirit barrels still work but only if the spirit is sent early - "Spirit barrels are still worth it because spirits will actually tank for the barrel. In this case though, um the spirit is so slow it actually doesn't walk up in time" (clock 1:17-1:09).

Result: regular time expires 0-0 on towers (own 2067/2248, enemy 2013/1611); in overtime the barrel plus Wall Breakers pressure switches to the left lane and takes the enemy left tower from 2013 to 630 before the game ends at overtime 1:05 - "Wall Breakers the barrel. The Wall Breakers. Let's go. Good game."

new_deck.display_name: Ryley Hero Berserker Log Bait (Goblin Barrel / Wall Breakers)
new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers, Dart Goblin and two spirits all bait the same small spells and cheap answers, and Ryley calls it "this bait deck" and "log bait" himself, but at 2.4 average elixir every deployment is bridge pressure in alternating lanes.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The list is the standard Goblin Barrel / Wall Breakers bait shell with the Hero Berserker replacing the usual mini-tank: a 2 Elixir body that, with Savage Survival for 3 more, cannot be killed for four seconds and shreds the swarm answering a push. That gives a 2.4 Elixir bait deck a defensive trump it normally does not have, which matters because the deck's only other defensive anchors are one Tesla and one Royal Delivery. Offence is pure two-lane pressure - barrel one tower, Wall Breakers the other, a spirit tanking for the barrel and the Dart Goblin left deep to defend rather than support. The weak point in this match was cycle: Ryley says repeatedly he is being out-cycled and cannot afford to defend Wall Breakers cleanly, and the post-nerf spirits no longer walk up fast enough to tank for the barrel, so the deck has to win on volume of chip rather than on clean value trades.
